takeaway: Posterior triangle of the neck: posterior border of sternocleidomastoid anteriorly, anterior border of trapezius posteriorly, middle third of clavicle as the base.

question.text: A 23-year-old woman has a lump in the posterior triangle of the neck. Which structures form the boundaries of the posterior triangle?

answer.text: Posterior border of sternocleidomastoid, the clavicle and anterior border of trapezius

lines.text: The sternocleidomastoid divides the neck into anterior and posterior triangles.
The posterior triangle sits behind it.
Its front edge is the posterior border of sternocleidomastoid, the red rope.
Its back edge is the anterior border of trapezius, the blue rope.
The base is the middle third of the clavicle.
Our lump sits inside this triangle, so these three borders are the answer.
